title: Thoughts on the current situation of the Market
author: AhmedMostafa_dev
selftext:
We all have high-quality cameras on the backs of our phones, yet not all of us become filmmakers. Let's agree that no one can predict the future, but if we can learn one thing from history, it's that history keeps repeating itself.

Looking at the current boom in AI game development and the spread of what the community calls 'AI slop,' what truly needs to change is our distribution strategy. We need a 'TikTok for games'—a space where creators can make and share their games without strict quality gates or long verification queues that take longer than building the game itself. We need a free, accessible, fast-paced platform built for this new wave, much like what YouTube and TikTok did after cameras became ubiquitous. Not everyone needed to make cinema or wait months to get a 30-second reel onto the big screen. We should build a platform capable of absorbing this massive wave of production and turning it into a profitable model for both creators and the platform whenever a game is fun and engaging for players.

I would love to hear from you.

comments.author: FlashMcSuave
comments.body:
There are a whole lot of factors affecting this and I don't think this actually tackles the key problems. 

Ultimately, what we are talking about here is the attention economy. It's what the entire tech sector runs on - advertising and data collection. It's all about attention. 

AI has enabled a lot more content to be produced but much of it tends to be towards the lower end of the quality spectrum. Of course AI can be used to create great things with a lot of human supervision, but the immediate applications are, well, slop. That's what can be easily mass produced, whereas quality can't. 

You are suggesting that the current mechanisms don't allow for enough volume to be pushed out the gate to get attention. 

I am saying that attention from gamers is a limited resource, and that when you reduce the barriers to pushing out material, you will simply exponentially increase the amount of slop without the corresponding increase in attention. 

The attention is the shortage. There isn't enough of it currently. A new platform won't fix that.

comments.author: ZeusGameAssets
comments.body:
The market is not the problem. People have been making slop games long before generative AI was here. It used to be called asset flipping, and a few decades before that, even the idea of using a game engine was considered cheating, and even today, some "veteran" game devs consider games made with Unity, Godot or Unreal to be slop.

The market has always been flooded with low effort games in some shape or form, with generative AI the barrier to entry is lower than ever, but making good games still matters. So the solution is to use every tool at your disposal to make better games.

Don't make slop, whether it's vibe coded, AI assisted, or purely human made. Pour effort in what you make, and try to make something of good quality. First you have to define what that good quality is, then set it as a target.
